assessment.summary: BTK (Q06187) is an exceptionally well-validated drug target with 170 PDB structures (best resolution 1.08Å), 21,674 ChEMBL IC50 entries (median 12 nM), and 6 approved drugs including ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib, and pirtobrutinib. The target has strong disease validation in B-cell malignancies and primary immunodeficiencies, with active ongoing research into next-generation inhibitors and PROTACs. Druggability is unambiguously high across all evidence dimensions.
evidence_gaps: Resistance mechanisms to covalent BTK inhibitors (e.g., C481S mutation) remain an active clinical challenge, though non-covalent inhibitors like pirtobrutinib partially address this
Long-term safety profiles of newer-generation BTK inhibitors (e.g., pirtobrutinib, PROTACs) are still being established in real-world settings
Selectivity profiles across the full kinome for all approved agents are not fully characterised, with off-target effects (e.g., ITK, TEC) contributing to some adverse events
PROTAC-based BTK degraders are still in early-stage discovery/clinical development with limited efficacy and safety data
Biomarker strategies for patient stratification and predicting BTK inhibitor response remain incompletely defined
